questions.question: Which of the following is the first solar project to break the grid parity barrier in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rewa Ultra Mega Solar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Grid parity is a time at which the electricity cost from the alternative source energy (such as PV or solar) cost is less than or equal to the electrical grid.**
 
• When the power generation is more than 500 MW, then it is called an ultra mega solar park.
 
• **Rewa solar project, set up in Madhya Pradesh becomes the first solar project to break the grid parity barrier in India. Hence option 3 is correct.**
 
 
• ​It is a 750 MW (three units generating 250 MW each) project which was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2020.
 
• **This project is estimated to reduce carbon dioxide emissions to 15 lakh tons per year.**
 
 
 
• It was developed by Rewa Ultra Mega Solar Ltd and Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park in Andhra Pradesh is the world's largest single location operational solar energy park with 1000 MW (250 MW power from each panel) power generation.**

 
 
• ​It was inaugurated by then Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu in Jan 2019.
 
 
 
• **Bhadla Solar Park located in Rajasthan is the world's largest solar park which has a capacity of 2.2 GW or 2240 MW.**
 
 
• ​It was commissioned in 2017 and has more than 10 mn solar panels.
 
 
 
• **Charanka Solar Park located in Gujarat generates around 600 MW** and was inaugurated n 2012 by then Chief Minister of Gujarat Narendra Modi.

questions.question: What does 'F' stand for in FRBM Act, 2003 of Indian economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The full form of the **FRBM Act is the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act.**
 
• The** 'F' in FRBM stands for Fiscal, **referring to government revenue, spending, and debt.
 
• The act was legislated by the **Government of India in 2003 to ensure fiscal discipline in the country.**
 
• The FRBM Act aims to eliminate revenue deficit and bring down fiscal deficit.
 
• This is achieved by** setting targets for the government's fiscal indicators like revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, and debt.**
 
• The act also restricts the government from borrowing from the **Reserve Bank of India, thereby ensuring financial stability.**
 
• The act encourages transparent **fiscal management systems in the country.**
 
• By **maintaining fiscal discipline, the act helps in controlling inflation and promoting economic stability.**

questions.question: Which of the following white papers, released by NITI Aayog, is related to Public Health Surveillance in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vision 2035**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vision 2035** is a white paper released by NITI Aayog focusing on the future of **Public Health Surveillance (PHS) in India**.
 
• The document outlines a strategy for **strengthening public health surveillance** systems to improve disease detection, monitoring, and response.
 
• It emphasizes the need for **integrated health information platforms** for real-time data sharing among healthcare providers and policymakers.
 
• The white paper envisions a shift from **reactive to proactive surveillance**, leveraging technology and data analytics.
 
• It aims to establish a robust public health surveillance system by **2035** to enhance India's capacity to prevent, detect, and respond to health emergencies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Health Surveillance:**

 
 
• It is the continuous, systematic collection, analysis, and interpretation of health-related data needed for planning, implementation, and evaluation of public health practice.
 
• Surveillance provides essential information for the control and prevention of disease outbreaks.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP):**
 
 
• An advanced information technology platform for disease surveillance in India.
 
• It aims to provide real-time data for early detection and management of disease outbreaks.
 
 
 
• **National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC):**
 
 
• A central organization responsible for monitoring and controlling disease outbreaks in India.
 
• It provides technical assistance to the states and union territories in the field of disease surveillance.
 
 
 
• **Digital Health Mission:**
 
 
• An initiative to create a digital health ecosystem in India.
 
• It includes the creation of a unique health ID for every citizen, digitization of health records, and development of registries for healthcare providers and facilities.
 
 
 
• **One Health Approach:**
 
 
• A collaborative effort of multiple disciplines working locally, nationally, and globally to achieve optimal health outcomes by recognizing the interconnection between people, animals, plants, and their shared environment.
 
• It is crucial for improving public health surveillance and combating zoonotic diseases.

questions.question: Who is the chairman of the State Planning Board?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Chief Minister** of a state serves as the chairman of the State Planning Board.
 
• The State Planning Board is an advisory body that provides input on the development plans of the state and ensures alignment with the state’s socio-economic objectives.
 
• It plays a key role in formulating the state's five-year and annual plans, while ensuring effective utilization of resources.
 
• The board consists of experts, officials, and non-official members, with the Chief Minister acting as its head.
 
• This institutional mechanism facilitates coordination between various departments and ensures that plans are consistent with the national development agenda.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State Planning Board:**

 
 
• It was established to decentralize planning and ensure state-specific needs are addressed effectively.
 
• The board works in tandem with the **NITI Aayog** at the central level to align state and national development goals.
 
• Its composition usually includes economists, social scientists, and government officials.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.
 
• It acts as a policy think tank for the Government of India, providing strategic and technical advice.
 
• The Prime Minister is the chairperson of NITI Aayog.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• India adopted the concept of five-year plans after independence, inspired by the Soviet model.
 
• The plans focus on economic growth, poverty alleviation, and social justice.
 
• The 12th Five-Year Plan (2012–2017) was the last such plan before the transition to NITI Aayog.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chief Minister:**
 
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the state government and oversees the administration of state departments.
 
• As the chairman of the State Planning Board, the Chief Minister ensures that development policies cater to the welfare of the state’s population.
 
• He/She also acts as a link between the state and the central government for funding and policy implementation.

questions.question: Poverty line measures poverty on the basis of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**income level or consumption expenditure**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Poverty is a certain category of people whose income cannot get the basic necessities of life.
 
• **The poverty line is used to categorize the people in above the poverty line and below the poverty line** i.e., those who can afford the basic necessities fall in the above poverty line and those who cannot, fall in the below poverty line and are considered economically poor.
 
• **The poverty line depends on the income of the households and their expenditure level. Hence option 4 is correct.**
 
• Earliest estimation of poverty was done by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book Un-British rule in India in the year 1867-68 and per capita income is estimated at 16 to 35 rupees. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tendulkar committee (2009), Lakdawala committee (1993), Alagh committee (1979)** etc are some of the committees that constituted for poverty estimation.
 
• **The poverty ration is one of the measures of poverty and is calculated by dividing the number of people below the poverty line (BPL) by the total population.**
 
 
• It is given by ​mathbf{(Households Below Poverty Line)/(Total Population)x100}.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Gap Index (PGI) is another tool for measuring poverty and it is the difference between the poverty line and the average income of all households below poverty line. **
 
 
• ​It is given by, mathbf{(Poverty Line-Average Income of Poor)/(Poverty Line)}

questions.question: Launched in 1951, India's first five-year plan was based on which of the following economic models to focus on agriculture and irrigation to boost farm output?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harrod-Domar Model.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• First Five Year Plan:

 
 
• The **first Indian prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru,** presented the** First Five-Year Plan** to the Parliament of India.
 
• The First Five-year Plan was launched in **1951** and mainly **focused** on the **development of the primary sector.**
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was based on the Harrod–Domar model with few modifications.
 
• The target growth rate was** 2.1%** annual gross domestic product (GDP) growth; the achieved growth rate was** 3.6%** the net domestic product went up by 15
 
• Many **irrigation projects** were initiated during this period, including the Bhakra, Hirakud, Mettur Dam, and Damodar Valley dams.
 
• At the end of the plan period in 1956, five Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) were started and The University Grants Commission (UGC) was set up.
 
• Contracts were signed to start five steel plants, which came into existence in the middle of the Second Five-Year Plan.
 
• The plan was **quasi-successful **for the government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Planning Commission, an agency of the government of India established in 1950 to oversee the country’s economic and social development, chiefly through the formulation of five-year plans.
 
• Five-year plan first-time was Introduced by Stalin in the Soviet region.
 
• First Five Year Plan(1951-1956):
 
 
• It is based on Harrod-Domar Model.
 
• It mainly focused on Agriculture.
 
• Community Development Program is also introduced in this Plan.
 
 
 
• Second Five Year Plan(1956-1961):
 
 
• It is based on Mahalanobis Model.
 
• It mainly focused on Industry.
 
• Steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela were established with the help of Russia, Britain (the U.K), and West Germany respectively.
 
 
 
• Fourth Five Year Plan(1969-1974):
 
 
• It is based on Ashok Rudra Alon Model.
 
• The smiling Buddha project was also introduced in this Plan.
 
• 14 Commercial Banks were also Nationalised in this Plan.
 
 
 
• Fifth Five-Year Plan(1974-1979):
 
 
• It is based on D.P.Dhar Model.
 
• The slogan "Garrebe Hatao" was also introduced in this plan.
 
• Regional Rural Bank was established In this Plan(2 October 1975).

questions.question: Which ministry organised a month-long programme called the 'Kashi Tamil Sangamam' in 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Ministry of Education.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Education:-**

 
 
• It is a government department or ministry responsible for overseeing and managing education policies, programs, and systems within a country or jurisdiction.
 
• **Its primary role is to ensure the provision of quality education and promote the development of human capital to meet the needs of the society and economy.**
 
• **Ministry of Education ​organised a month-long programme called the 'Kashi Tamil Sangamam' in 2022.**
 
• The specific responsibilities and functions of a Ministry of Education may vary from country to country, but some common areas they typically address include:
 
 
• **Educational Policies:** Formulating and implementing national or regional educational policies to guide the education system's direction and development.
 
• **Curriculum Development: **Designing and updating the curriculum to meet the educational goals and standards set by the government.
 
• **Teacher Training**: Establishing programs and initiatives to train and develop teachers, ensuring they have the necessary skills and qualifications to deliver quality education.
 
• **School Management: **Overseeing the administration and management of schools, including the allocation of resources and funding.
 
• **Education Quality Assurance: **Monitoring and evaluating the quality of education provided in schools and institutes to maintain high standards.
 
• **Education Funding:** Allocating and managing financial resources for educational institutions and programs.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Ministry of External Affairs:-**

 
 
• The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) is a government department or ministry responsible for managing a country's external relations and diplomatic affairs with other nations and international organizations.
 
• The primary role of the Ministry of External Affairs is to promote and protect the country's interests and values in the international arena. This ministry plays a crucial role in shaping foreign policy and representing the country's views on global issues.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Culture **
 
 
• The Ministry of Culture is a government department or ministry responsible for the promotion, preservation, and development of the country's cultural heritage, arts, and traditions.
 
• Its primary role is to nurture and safeguard the nation's cultural identity and diversity while fostering cultural exchanges and creative expressions both within the country and on the international stage.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Tribal Affairs **
 
 
• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is a government department or ministry in certain countries, particularly in India, dedicated to the welfare and development of tribal or indigenous communities.
 
• In India, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs was established to address the specific needs and concerns of the Scheduled Tribes (STs) or Adivasi communities and ensure their overall development and well-being.

questions.question: In 2023, Government of India has announced to set up a/an __________ DigiLocker for use by MSMEs, large businesses, and charitable trusts to store and share documents online securely.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Entity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2023, the Government of India announced the launch of an **Entity DigiLocker** for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), large businesses, and charitable trusts.
 
• The **Entity DigiLocker** aims to help organizations securely store and share official documents online.
 
• It is an extension of the existing DigiLocker platform, which was primarily designed for individual use.
 
• This initiative is part of India's broader push towards **digital governance** and ease of doing business.
 
• The platform ensures **data security** and compliance, providing users with a safe and reliable environment for document management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DigiLocker:**

 
 
• DigiLocker is a flagship initiative under the Digital India program by the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY).
 
• It allows Indian citizens to securely store and share digital documents, such as Aadhaar, PAN card, and educational certificates.
 
• Users can access their documents anytime, anywhere through the DigiLocker mobile app or website.
 
• The platform also supports government-to-citizen document issuance and verification.
 
 
 
• **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs):**
 
 
• MSMEs are classified based on investment in plant/machinery or equipment and annual turnover.
 
• They contribute significantly to India’s GDP, exports, and employment generation.
 
• The government provides various schemes to support MSMEs, such as credit assistance, skill development, and technology upgradation.
 
 
 
• **Digital Governance in India:**
 
 
• Digital governance refers to the use of digital technologies to enhance the delivery of government services to citizens and businesses.
 
• Programs like Digital India aim to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
 
• Key initiatives include Aadhaar, e-Governance projects, and the Unified Payments Interface (UPI).
 
 
 
• **Charitable Trusts:**
 
 
• Charitable trusts in India operate for philanthropic purposes, such as education, healthcare, and poverty alleviation.
 
• They are registered under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, and are eligible for tax benefits under the Income Tax Act.
 
• The Entity DigiLocker offers a streamlined way for trusts to manage and share compliance-related documents.
